沙市堂 主日崇拜 · Shashi Church Sunday Worship

2026年10月4日（主日）· Sunday 4 October 2026 · 上午 9:00
主礼 Presiding: 段光霞 传道 (evangelist) · 证道 Sermon: 丁江华 牧师 (pastor)
晚堂 Evening service 19:00 at 香榭丽都聚会点 (江津中路, opposite RT-Mart 大润发): 主礼 张强 传道 · 证道 丁江华 牧师
圣餐 Holy Communion today (item 12) — 信徒同立: baptized believers stand to receive.
温馨提示 After the service: 灵命栽培课程 (a discipleship / spiritual-nurture class) in the 2nd-floor classroom.

This is the Sunday of the 国庆节 National Day holiday week (1 October was Thursday): the choir sings《我爱中国教会歌》I Love the Church in China and the congregation《为国求福歌》Prayer for Our Country. The order has 19 items, one more than last Sunday, because of Communion.

今日主题 · Today’s Theme

基督徒的责任 — the Christian’s responsibility. The sermon series reaches the last instructions of Colossians (4:2–6). After the new clothes (3:12–17, two weeks ago) and the new household (3:18–4:1, last week), Paul turns the church to face outward, in three short commands that the bulletin’s outline follows exactly: 恒切祷告 keep on praying — watchfully, thankfully, and for the preachers too (vv. 2–4); 智慧行事 act wisely toward 外人 “outsiders”, making the most of the time (v. 5); 言语柔和 speak graciously, 好像用盐调和 “as if seasoned with salt”, so as to know how to answer each person (v. 6). Paul writes this in chains (我为此被捆锁), and what he asks prayer for is not his release but an open door for the message.

The three lessons are all about answering for oneself. 以西结 Ezekiel forbids the exiles’ proverb about sour grapes — no one may blame the parents; each person stands before God, and the invitation is 回头而存活 “turn, and live”. 保罗 Paul sets out the mind of Christ, who emptied himself and obeyed to the point of death, and then says 做成你们得救的工夫 “work out your salvation” — because God is at work in you. And in 马太福音 Matthew Jesus tells of two sons: one said “I will not” and went; the other said “I go, sir” and did not. Responsibility, in all three, is not what one says but what one turns and does. The psalm (25) gives the prayer underneath it: 求你将你的道指示我 — show me your ways.

Today is also a Communion Sunday, and the opening hymn was written for Communion: “For the Beauty of the Earth” first ended every stanza “Christ, our God, to Thee we raise this our sacrifice of praise.”

Lectionary note: Ezekiel 18:1–4, 25–32, Ps 25, Phil 2:1–13 and Matt 21:23–32 are the Revised Common Lectionary set for Year A, Proper 21 (the church again runs one week behind the RCL calendar); Colossians 4:2–6 continues its own sermon series. In many churches abroad the first Sunday of October is kept as World Communion Sunday.

逐项解读 · Walk-Through ↑

1 · 序乐 Prelude — 众立·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Silence first — the service begins by listening. Hymns are from《赞美诗（新编）》(the 1983 Chinese New Hymnal, 400 hymns); numbers are announced as 赞美诗第…首.

Organ/piano prelude while the 诗班 (choir), 主礼人 (presider) and 证道人 (preacher) process in. Everyone stands and keeps silent.

2 · 问安 Greeting — 赞美诗 396《主在圣殿中》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: “The Lord is in his holy temple” — the same stillness the whole service asks for before God speaks.

♪ 五线谱 score →

Sung softly as an introit (哈巴谷书 Habakkuk 2:20); music by George F. Root (1820–1895). After it the presider greets: 弟兄姊妹，主内平安！ — the congregation answers 平安！

主在圣殿中，主在圣殿中，普天下的人，在主面前都应当肃静，肃静，肃静，应当肃静。阿们。
The Lord is in His holy temple, the Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence, let all the earth keep silence before Him; keep silence, keep silence before Him. Amen.

3 · 宣召 Call to Worship — 诗篇 Psalm 25:1–5 · 众立 ↑

主题 Theme: “Show me your ways” — a prayer to be taught and led, before a sermon about what a Christian is answerable for.

1 耶和华啊，我的心仰望你。
1 To you, Yahweh, do I lift up my soul.
2 我的神啊，我素来倚靠你；求你不要叫我羞愧，不要叫我的仇敌向我夸胜。
2 My God, I have trusted in you. Don’t let me be shamed. Don’t let my enemies triumph over me.
3 凡等候你的必不羞愧；惟有那无故行奸诈的必要羞愧。
3 Yes, no one who waits for you shall be shamed. They shall be shamed who deal treacherously without cause.
4 耶和华啊，求你将你的道指示我，将你的路教训我！
4 Show me your ways, Yahweh. Teach me your paths.
5 求你以你的真理引导我，教训我，因为你是救我的神。我终日等候你。
5 Guide me in your truth, and teach me, For you are the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.

背景 Background. Psalm 25 is a prayer of David for guidance and forgiveness and, like last week’s Psalm 145, an alphabet psalm: each verse begins with the next Hebrew letter. Two words carry these five verses. 等候 “wait” (vv. 3, 5): those who wait for God are not put to shame, and the psalmist waits 终日 all day long. And 道 / 路 “way / path” (v. 4): 求你将你的道指示我 show me your ways, 将你的路教训我 teach me your paths. Keep that word 道 in your ear — in the first lesson the exiles complain 主的道不公平 “the way of the Lord is not fair”, and in the Gospel John comes 遵着义路 “in the way of righteousness”. Also listen for 倚靠 trust, 羞愧 shame, 仇敌 enemies, 真理 truth, 引导 guide.

4 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 26《大地风光歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Thanksgiving for creation and for the people we are given — 感恩, the word the sermon text attaches to prayer (Col 4:2) — in a hymn first written for Communion.

♪ 五线谱 score →

“For the Beauty of the Earth.” Words by Folliott Sandford Pierpoint (1835–1917), written near Bath in 1864 and published that year as a Communion hymn, with the refrain “Christ, our God, to Thee we raise this our sacrifice of praise”; most hymnals now print “Lord of all, to Thee we raise this our hymn of grateful praise”, and the Chinese follows that form. The tune is DIX, which William Henry Monk adapted in 1861 from a chorale by Conrad Kocher (1838) — the same tune as “As with Gladness Men of Old”. Chinese by 刘廷芳 (Timothy Tingfang Lew) 1933 for 普天颂赞 Hymns of Universal Praise. Four of Pierpoint’s eight stanzas: earth and sky, day and night, ear and eye, human love. A-flat major, 4/4. Stanza 4, with its 祖宗 ancestors, 父母 parents and 兄弟姊妹 brothers and sisters, suits a holiday week when families are together.

1. 环观大地好风光，仰视美丽好穹苍，想起坠地到如今，挚爱时常绕我旁。
2. 静观昼夜每时间，色色形形美丽中，绿水青山描写巧，日月星辰点缀工。
3. 主赐耳聪目亦明，欢愉充满健精神，更赐神秘和谐趣，声色由空转化真。
4. 祖宗遗泽父母爱，兄弟姊妹犹手足，人间天上友朋多，爱久情深长享乐。
副歌 Refrain: 敬向全能万有神，献上颂扬感谢心。阿们。

1. For the beauty of the earth, for the glory of the skies, for the love which from our birth over and around us lies:
2. For the wonder of each hour of the day and of the night, hill and vale and tree and flower, sun and moon and stars of light:
3. For the joy of ear and eye, for the heart and mind’s delight, for the mystic harmony linking sense to sound and sight:
4. For the joy of human love, brother, sister, parent, child, friends on earth and friends above, for all gentle thoughts and mild:
Refrain: Lord of all, to Thee we raise this our hymn of grateful praise.

5 · 祷告 Prayer — 众立·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: The opening prayer usually includes confession — fitting on a Communion Sunday, when Paul asks each person to examine himself first (1 Cor 11:28).

The presider’s opening prayer: praise, confession, and asking God’s presence on the service. Stand quietly; join in the closing 阿们.

6 · 宣信 Confession of Faith — 赞美诗 395《使徒信经》· 众立·同诵 ↑

主题 Theme: 我信圣而公之教会 — “the holy catholic Church”: the one church the choir is about to sing of, and the one table of Communion.

♪ 五线谱 score →

The Apostles’ Creed, recited together (hymnal 395 also prints John Stainer’s chant setting). 上帝 here and 神 in the Bible text are both “God” — the hymnal’s and the 和合本 神-edition’s conventions.

我信上帝，全能的父，创造天地的主。我信我主耶稣基督，上帝独生的子；因圣灵感孕，由童贞女马利亚所生；在本丢彼拉多手下受难，被钉于十字架，受死，埋葬；降在阴间，第三天从死人中复活；升天，坐在全能父上帝的右边；将来必从那里降临，审判活人死人。我信圣灵；我信圣而公之教会；我信圣徒相通；我信罪得赦免；我信身体复活；我信永生。阿们。

I believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. I believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died, and was buried; he descended to the dead. On the third day he rose again; he ascended into heaven, he is seated at the right hand of the Father, and he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.

7 · 诗班献唱 Choir Anthem — 赞美诗 127《我爱中国教会歌》· 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: In National Day week the choir sings of love for the church in this country — a 金灯台 golden lampstand, one in Christ.

“I Love the Church in China.” A Chinese original written for the New Hymnal: words by 史奇珪 (Shi Qigui) and 孙定武, 1981; music by 史奇珪, 1981. Section: 教会生活·教会·团契 (church life — church and fellowship). E-flat major, 4/4 with a single 2/4 bar, four stanzas and a refrain. The choir sings; the congregation sits and listens.

What it says. Each stanza opens by naming what the heavenly Father (天父) does for “our church” — he leads it, cares for it, blesses it, shows it favour — and each ends with the same promise, “I will follow for ever”. Stanza 1 names the Three-Self principle: 自治 self-governing, 自养 self-supporting, 自传 self-propagating. Stanza 2 quotes Ephesians 4:5: 一主 one Lord, 一信 one faith, 一洗 one baptism. The refrain calls the church a 金灯台 golden lampstand (Revelation 1:20) and prays that it be 合而为一 made one (John 17:21), loving one another, with the Lord present always.

The words of this hymn are still in copyright, so they are not reproduced here; follow them in the hymnal, no. 127 (page 127 of the staff-notation PDF).

8 · 经训 Scripture Lessons — 会众同应 (responsive) ↑

主题 Theme: Three pictures of answering for oneself: the exile who may not blame his father, the Christ who obeyed to the cross, and the son who said no and went.

Read responsively — the leader reads a verse and the congregation the next, or the congregation reads together.

以西结书 Ezekiel 18:1–4, 25–32 — 回头而存活 Turn, and live ↑

1 耶和华的话又临到我说：
1 Yahweh’s word came to me again, saying,
2 「你们在以色列地怎么用这俗语说『父亲吃了酸葡萄，儿子的牙酸倒了』呢？」
2 “What do you mean, that you use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge’?
3 主耶和华说：「我指着我的永生起誓，你们在以色列中，必不再有用这俗语的因由。
3 “As I live,” says the Lord Yahweh, “you shall not use this proverb any more in Israel.
4 看哪，世人都是属我的；为父的怎样属我，为子的也照样属我；犯罪的，他必死亡。
4 Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul who sins, he shall die.
… verses 5–24 are not read …
25 「你们还说：『主的道不公平！』以色列家啊，你们当听，我的道岂不公平吗？你们的道岂不是不公平吗？
25 “Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not equal.’ Hear now, house of Israel: Is my way not equal? Aren’t your ways unequal?
26 义人若转离义行而作罪孽死亡，他是因所作的罪孽死亡。
26 When the righteous man turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity, and dies therein; in his iniquity that he has done he shall die.
27 再者，恶人若回头离开所行的恶，行正直与合理的事，他必将性命救活了。
27 Again, when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed, and does that which is lawful and right, he will save his soul alive.
28 因为他思量，回头离开所犯的一切罪过，必定存活，不致死亡。
28 Because he considers, and turns away from all his transgressions that he has committed, he shall surely live. He shall not die.
29 以色列家还说：『主的道不公平！』以色列家啊，我的道岂不公平吗？你们的道岂不是不公平吗？」
29 Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not fair.’ House of Israel, aren’t my ways fair? Aren’t your ways unfair?
30 所以主耶和华说：「以色列家啊，我必按你们各人所行的审判你们。你们当回头离开所犯的一切罪过。这样，罪孽必不使你们败亡。
30 “Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ways,” says the Lord Yahweh. “Return, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity will not be your ruin.
31 你们要将所犯的一切罪过尽行抛弃，自做一个新心和新灵。以色列家啊，你们何必死亡呢？
31 Cast away from you all your transgressions, in which you have transgressed; and make yourself a new heart and a new spirit: for why will you die, house of Israel?
32 主耶和华说：我不喜悦那死人之死，所以你们当回头而存活。」
32 For I have no pleasure in the death of him who dies,” says the Lord Yahweh. “Therefore turn yourselves, and live!

背景 Background. 以西结 Ezekiel was a priest carried off to Babylon in 597 BC; he speaks to exiles who explain their disaster with a 俗语 proverb: 父亲吃了酸葡萄，儿子的牙酸倒了 — the fathers ate sour grapes and the children’s teeth are set on edge (Jeremiah 31:29 quotes it too). We suffer, they mean, for what our parents did. God forbids the proverb: 世人都是属我的 every life belongs to me, father and son alike; 犯罪的，他必死亡 the one who sins is the one who dies. The verses skipped today (5–24) work this through three generations — a righteous man, his violent son, and a grandson who sees it and does otherwise. Then the exiles’ complaint, 主的道不公平 “the Lord’s way is not fair”, is turned back on them: a righteous person who turns away (转离) dies, a wicked person who turns back (回头) lives. The chapter ends not with a verdict but with an appeal: 你们何必死亡呢？ why should you die? 我不喜悦那死人之死 I take no pleasure in anyone’s death; 所以你们当回头而存活 so turn, and live. Listen for 罪孽 iniquity, 罪过 offences, 审判 judge, 回头 turn back, 存活 live, and 新心 … 新灵 “a new heart and a new spirit” — commanded here, promised as a gift in 36:26.

腓立比书 Philippians 2:1–13 — 以基督耶稣的心为心 The mind of Christ ↑

1 所以，在基督里若有甚么劝勉，爱心有甚么安慰，圣灵有甚么交通，心中有甚么慈悲怜悯，
1 If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,
2 你们就要意念相同，爱心相同，有一样的心思，有一样的意念，使我的喜乐可以满足。
2 make my joy full, by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
3 凡事不可结党，不可贪图虚浮的荣耀；只要存心谦卑，各人看别人比自己强。
3 doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
4 各人不要单顾自己的事，也要顾别人的事。
4 each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
5 你们当以基督耶稣的心为心：
5 Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,
6 他本有神的形像，不以自己与神同等为强夺的；
6 who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
7 反倒虚己，取了奴仆的形像，成为人的样式；
7 but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
8 既有人的样子，就自己卑微，存心顺服，以至于死，且死在十字架上。
8 And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, yes, the death of the cross.
9 所以，神将他升为至高，又赐给他那超乎万名之上的名，
9 Therefore God also highly exalted him, and gave to him the name which is above every name;
10 叫一切在天上的、地上的，和地底下的，因耶稣的名无不屈膝，
10 that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
11 无不口称「耶稣基督为主」，使荣耀归与父神。
11 and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
12 这样看来，我亲爱的弟兄，你们既是常顺服的，不但我在你们那里，就是我如今不在你们那里，更是顺服的，就当恐惧战兢做成你们得救的工夫。
12 So then, my beloved, even as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
13 因为你们立志行事都是神在你们心里运行，为要成就他的美意。
13 For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.

背景 Background. This follows straight on from last week’s lesson (1:21–30), where Paul, in prison, asked the Philippians to stand firm 同有一个心志 in one spirit. Now he says how: 存心谦卑 humility, 各人看别人比自己强 counting others better than oneself. Verses 6–11 are often thought to be an early hymn that Paul is quoting. It goes down and then up: Christ had 神的形像 the form of God, yet 虚己 emptied himself, took 奴仆的形像 the form of a slave, and was 顺服 obedient 以至于死 to the point of death — 且死在十字架上 even death on a cross; therefore God raised him 至高 to the highest, so that every knee should bow (无不屈膝) and every tongue confess 耶稣基督为主 “Jesus Christ is Lord”. Then the sentence that ties the lesson to today’s sermon title: 就当恐惧战兢做成你们得救的工夫 work out your salvation with fear and trembling — 因为 … 都是神在你们心里运行 for it is God who works in you. Responsibility and grace in one breath. Two words that have shifted since 1919: 甚么 is today’s 什么 “what / any”, and 交通 here means “fellowship” (Greek koinonia, the word behind “communion”), though in the street it now means traffic.

马太福音 Matthew 21:23–32 — 两个儿子的比喻 The two sons ↑

23 耶稣进了殿，正教训人的时候，祭司长和民间的长老来问他说：「你仗着甚么权柄做这些事？给你这权柄的是谁呢？」
23 When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
24 耶稣回答说：「我也要问你们一句话，你们若告诉我，我就告诉你们我仗着甚么权柄做这些事。
24 Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
25 约翰的洗礼是从哪里来的？是从天上来的？是从人间来的呢？」他们彼此商议说：「我们若说『从天上来』，他必对我们说：『这样，你们为甚么不信他呢？』
25 The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?” They reasoned with themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will ask us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
26 若说『从人间来』，我们又怕百姓，因为他们都以约翰为先知。」
26 But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”
27 于是回答耶稣说：「我们不知道。」耶稣说：「我也不告诉你们我仗着甚么权柄做这些事。」
27 They answered Jesus, and said, “We don’t know.” He also said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
28 又说：「一个人有两个儿子。他来对大儿子说：『我儿，你今天到葡萄园里去做工。』
28 But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’
29 他回答说：『我不去』，以后自己懊悔，就去了。
29 He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.
30 又来对小儿子也是这样说。他回答说：『父啊，我去』，他却不去。
30 He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.
31 你们想，这两个儿子是哪一个遵行父命呢？」他们说：「大儿子。」耶稣说：「我实在告诉你们，税吏和娼妓倒比你们先进神的国。
31 Which of the two did the will of his father?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.
32 因为约翰遵着义路到你们这里来，你们却不信他；税吏和娼妓倒信他。你们看见了，后来还是不懊悔去信他。」
32 For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.

背景 Background. Jerusalem, in the last week: Jesus has entered the city and driven the traders out of the temple, and the 祭司长 chief priests and 长老 elders ask by what 权柄 authority he acts. He answers with a question about 约翰的洗礼 John’s baptism — from heaven or from men? — and they will not commit themselves: 我们不知道 “we do not know”. Then the parable. A father asks two sons to work in the 葡萄园 vineyard (the same vineyard as last week’s labourers). The first says 我不去 “I will not go”, then 懊悔 thinks better of it and goes; the second says 父啊，我去 “I go, sir”, and does not. Which one 遵行父命 did the father’s will? The leaders give the right answer and convict themselves: 税吏和娼妓 the tax collectors and prostitutes believed John and are going into God’s kingdom ahead of them. This is Ezekiel’s point told as a story — the one who turns (回头) lives, whatever was said at first.

9 · 读经 Sermon Text — 歌罗西书 Colossians 4:2–6 · 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: Pray, walk, speak — the letter’s last three instructions, all facing outward.

2 你们要恒切祷告，在此警醒感恩。
2 Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching therein with thanksgiving;
3 也要为我们祷告，求神给我们开传道的门，能以讲基督的奥秘（我为此被捆锁），
3 praying together for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds;
4 叫我按着所该说的话将这奥秘发明出来。
4 that I may reveal it as I ought to speak.
5 你们要爱惜光阴，用智慧与外人交往。
5 Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.
6 你们的言语要常常带着和气，好像用盐调和，就可知道该怎样回答各人。
6 Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.

背景 Background. These five verses close the body of the letter; after them come only personal news and greetings (4:7–18). Prayer (vv. 2–4): 恒切 is “steadfast, persevering” (恒 constant + 切 earnest); 警醒 “watchful”, the word Jesus used in Gethsemane; and 感恩 “with thanksgiving”, a note this letter keeps sounding (3:15–17 last time). Paul then asks for prayer for himself — he is 被捆锁 in chains — and what he wants opened is not his cell but 传道的门 “a door for the word”, so that he can make the 奥秘 mystery of Christ plain. (CUV’s 发明 here is the old sense, “bring to light”, not the modern “invent”.) Conduct (v. 5): 用智慧与外人交往 “walk in wisdom toward outsiders” — 外人 are those outside the church — and 爱惜光阴, literally “treasure the time”: buy up every opportunity. Speech (v. 6): 常常带着和气 always gracious (和气 is the everyday word for a friendly, even-tempered manner), 好像用盐调和 seasoned with salt — neither tasteless nor harsh — so as to know how to 回答各人 answer each person. The bulletin’s outline sums up the three as 恒切祷告, 智慧行事 and 言语柔和.

10 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 175《为国求福歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Sung between the text and the sermon: prayer for the nation in National Day week — the first of the three duties, 恒切祷告, put into practice at once.

♪ 五线谱 score →

“Prayer for Our Country.” Words by 戚瀛茂 (the hymnal gives his dates as 1841–1911); the melody is a traditional Chinese tune arranged by 苏路熙 Lucy Soothill (d. 1931), who with her husband W. E. Soothill served the Methodist mission in Wenzhou and set hymns to Chinese melodies. Section: 教会生活·为国求福 (church life — prayer for the nation), the same section as last week’s anthem. G major, 4/4, two short lines to a stanza; the tune is pentatonic and easy to pick up. Notice the order of the prayer: first 万国万族 all nations and peoples, then 我国 my own country.

1. 求主眷顾万国万族，仁慈遍及四方，更为我国求主赐福，永远常被恩光。
2. 此处有我先贤列祖，原是我家故里，有我亲友兄弟父母，别处那能相比？
3. 为此求主保全我国，可以广行仁政，令我本国众民同乐，土地所产丰盛。
4. 我愿本国人民安泰，家家永无困苦，同守律法彼此相爱，靠赖全能恩主。阿们。

Sense of the stanzas: 1 — Lord, look kindly on every nation and people and let your mercy reach the four quarters; and for my own country too I ask your blessing, that it may always live in the light of your grace. 2 — Here lived my forebears and the worthies of old; this is my family’s home, where my relatives, friends, brothers and parents are — how could anywhere else compare? 3 — So keep my country safe, Lord, that good government may spread, its people be glad together and the land give its increase. 4 — May its people live in peace and no home be in want; may we keep the law and love one another, relying on the almighty Lord of grace.

11 · 证道 Sermon —《基督徒的责任》· 丁江华 牧师 · 众坐·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Expect the claim that faith carries duties that face outward — to pray for others, to live wisely among those who do not believe, and to speak well.

“The Christian’s Responsibility” (基督徒 Christian · 责任 responsibility, duty). Text: Colossians 4:2–6. The preacher is 丁江华 牧师, who also preaches at the evening service; the presider, 段光霞 传道, led last Sunday’s evening service.

证道大纲 Sermon outline (from the bulletin):

一、应当恒切祷告 (2–4节)
1. We should persevere in prayer (应当 should; 恒切 steadfast, earnest) — vv. 2–4.
二、应当智慧行事 (5节)
2. We should act with wisdom (智慧 wisdom; 行事 to act, conduct oneself) — v. 5.
三、应当言语柔和 (6节)
3. We should be gentle in speech (言语 speech; 柔和 gentle, mild) — v. 6.

What to expect under each point. Point 1 — prayer that does not give up (恒切), stays awake (警醒) and gives thanks (感恩); and 代祷 intercession: Paul’s 也要为我们祷告 “pray for us too” will probably become prayer for pastors, for the church and for the gospel’s open door (传道的门). Point 2 — 外人 “outsiders” applied to family, neighbours and colleagues who do not believe; 智慧 wisdom in how one lives among them; 爱惜光阴 not wasting time or opportunity; the Christian’s life as a 见证 witness. Point 3 — 和气 graciousness and 盐 salt; quite possibly 马太福音 Matthew 5:13 (你们是世上的盐 “you are the salt of the earth”) and 1 Peter 3:15 on answering everyone gently. Since Communion follows directly, expect the close to turn toward the table.

See 讲道关键词 Sermon key words in the phrases section below.

12 · 圣餐 Holy Communion — 信徒同立 ↑

主题 Theme: 为的是记念我 — “do this in remembrance of me.” The bulletin’s direction is 信徒同立: the believers stand together.

Communion was not in last Sunday’s order; Chinese Protestant churches usually keep it once a month, most often on the first Sunday. Details differ from church to church, but the usual pattern is this. The pastor comes to the table and reads Paul’s account of the Last Supper (哥林多前书 1 Corinthians 11:23–26, below), often with the verses that follow about examining oneself (自己省察, v. 28). Those who will receive stand — that is the 信徒同立 on the bulletin — while others stay seated. The pastor gives thanks over the 饼 bread and then the 杯 cup; helpers bring them along the rows, small pieces of bread and small individual cups; everyone holds theirs and eats, then drinks, together at the pastor’s word. A hymn may be sung softly meanwhile.

For a visitor. In China’s churches Communion is for the baptized (受洗 to be baptized; 信徒 here means baptized members); people who have not been baptized simply remain seated, and no one minds. A baptized Christian from another church is normally welcome. If you are unsure, ask someone beforehand: 我在美国受过洗，可以领圣餐吗？ “I was baptized in America — may I receive Communion?”

23 我当日传给你们的，原是从主领受的，就是主耶稣被卖的那一夜，拿起饼来，
23 For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.
24 祝谢了，就擘开，说：「这是我的身体，为你们舍的，你们应当如此行，为的是记念我。」
24 When he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”
25 饭后，也照样拿起杯来，说：「这杯是用我的血所立的新约，你们每逢喝的时候，要如此行，为的是记念我。」
25 In the same way he also took the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”
26 你们每逢吃这饼，喝这杯，是表明主的死，直等到他来。
26 For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

13 · 堂务报告 Announcements — 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: The week’s chances to pray together and to 爱惜光阴 use the time well.

This week’s bulletin: 灵命栽培课程 (spiritual-nurture / discipleship class) after the service in the 2nd-floor classroom (二楼教室). Regular meetings, unchanged from last week: Tuesday 6:30–7:30 晨更祷告 morning prayer (沙市堂); Wednesday 14:00–16:00 查经 Bible study at the 北湖, 东区, 香榭丽都 and 石油学院 meeting points; Saturday 8:00–10:30 诗班 choir rehearsal; Sunday 19:00–21:00 香榭丽都 evening worship. Small groups (小组): 迦勒 Caleb (Tue 19:00, 香榭丽都); 得鱼 Fishers, 芥菜种 Mustard Seed, 但以理 Daniel, 玛利亚 Mary (Fri 19:00, 沙市堂). Expect holiday greetings: 国庆节快乐.

14 · 欢迎第一次来的朋友 Welcome to First-Time Visitors — 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: 用智慧与外人交往 — the sermon’s second point, practised on the spot: how the church receives those who have just walked in.

Visitors are usually asked to stand (or raise a hand) and are welcomed with applause. A smile, a nod and 谢谢 / 主内平安 is plenty; you may be asked 从哪里来 “where are you from?”.

15 · 祷告 Prayer — 为有需要者祷告 · 众坐·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Intercession for the sick and grieving — 也要为我们祷告, “pray for us too”, is what the text has just asked.

Seated, in silence; close with 阿们.

16 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 366《光照小地方歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: The response to the sermon: responsibility begins where you are standing. The Chinese first stanza even uses the sermon’s word, 责任 — the duties already in front of you.

“Brighten the Corner Where You Are.” Words by Ina Duley Ogdon (1872–1964), written in 1913 after she gave up a place on the Chautauqua lecture circuit to stay home and care for her father; music by Charles H. Gabriel (1856–1932). Homer Rodeheaver made it the theme song of Billy Sunday’s revival meetings. Chinese by 刘廷芳 and 杨荫浏, 1933, for 普天颂赞. Section: 信徒灵修·忠心服务 (devotion — faithful service). E-flat major, 4/4, three stanzas with a refrain; the Chinese keeps the bouncing dotted rhythm of the original.

1. Do not wait until some deed of greatness you may do, do not wait to shed your light afar; to the many duties ever near you now be true, brighten the corner where you are.
2. Just above are clouded skies that you may help to clear, let not narrow self your way debar; though into one heart alone may fall your song of cheer, brighten the corner where you are.
3. Here for all your talent you may surely find a need, here reflect the bright and Morning Star; even from your humble hand the Bread of Life may feed, brighten the corner where you are.
Refrain: Brighten the corner where you are! Brighten the corner where you are! Someone far from harbor you may guide across the bar; brighten the corner where you are!

Following the Chinese. The translation keeps close to the English, stanza for stanza. The title line, sung at the end of every stanza and three times in the refrain, is 光照你所在小地方 — 光照 shine on, 你所在 where you are, 小地方 the small place. Other words to catch: 大事 great deeds, 远方 far away, 眼前 right in front of you, 责任 duties, 力量 strength; in the refrain 海面 the sea, 船 a ship, 平安 safely, 进港 enter the harbour.

The Chinese translation is still in copyright (杨荫浏 died in 1984), so it is not reproduced here; sing from the hymnal, no. 366 (page 371 of the staff-notation PDF). Ogdon’s English is in the public domain.

17 · 主祷文 The Lord’s Prayer — 马太福音 Matthew 6:9–13 · 众立·同诵 ↑

主题 Theme: 我们日用的饮食，今日赐给我们 — “give us today our daily bread”, said minutes after the bread of Communion.

我们在天上的父，愿人都尊你的名为圣。愿你的国降临，愿你的旨意行在地上，如同行在天上。我们日用的饮食，今日赐给我们。免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债。不叫我们遇见试探，救我们脱离凶恶。因为国度、权柄、荣耀，全是你的，直到永远。阿们。

Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.

18 · 祝福 Benediction — 众立 ↑

主题 Theme: 赐你平安 — sent out with peace, toward the 外人 the sermon spoke of.

Usually one of these two:

民数记 Numbers 6:24–26: 愿耶和华赐福给你，保护你。愿耶和华使他的脸光照你，赐恩给你。愿耶和华向你仰脸，赐你平安。
The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine on you and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up his countenance on you and give you peace.

哥林多后书 2 Corinthians 13:14: 愿主耶稣基督的恩惠、神的慈爱、圣灵的感动，常与你们众人同在！
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

19 · 阿们颂 Amen — 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: “So be it” — then out to your own corner.

The three-fold sung Amen (hymnal 400). Then the choir and ministers recess; greet people with 主内平安, and this week 国庆节快乐 (happy National Day).
